x: A brown healthy looking Gerry North---freshly returned from Mexico---was out to see whether he could do a "Keino"; having descended over 17,000 feet a few days earlier.

Kipchoge Steer, complete with a Keino type sun-cap, descended to sea level Battersea from the Kensington heights to run in the 2 miles. But despite flinging aside his hat for the last lap, both he and Gerry North cantered in together for an easy 9:45.

CENTRE:Keino (Ken) beats Ryun (USA) by a 'street' to take 1500m. BOTTOM:The medallist the Americans rated second only to Beamon; Britain's Dave Hemery caught in flight down the final straight of the 400 metres hurdles in a world record of 48.1 seconds.

But it's not surprising really as his father is Tom O'Riordan, the first Irishman to run inside 14 minutes for 5k back in the 'sixties, a competitor who proudly bore his emerald green singlet in the Tokyo Olympics of 1964 alongside some great names - Jazy, Keino, Clarke.
